# Process — the rules in force

Loaded with `/scope`, `/step`, `/steps`, `/ship`, `/new-adr`, `/bootstrap` and any review pass. Each line names the record it comes from; open that record when the line is not enough. Which window is open and which records are in force is stated once, in [the ledger](../plan/README.md#the-window).

- **Deliverables** — Work is staged into numbered deliverables, one plan file each, steps written `D<n>.<step>`. One deliverable is in progress at a time, and it closes on an executable acceptance checklist. — [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-deliverables.md) (deliverables) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md)
- **The window** — An ADR may be amended in place only while the deliverable it belongs to is in progress; once that deliverable ships the record changes only by supersession. Which window is open, and which records are in force, is stated in one place — the ledger — and linked from everywhere else. — [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-deliverables.md) (deliverables) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md)
- **Acceptance at the head** — A record written `proposed` is accepted at the head of the step that builds it, so a step whose record is still `proposed` is gated and must not be started. — [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-deliverables.md) (deliverables) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md)
- **Supersession states the delta** — A superseding record states the delta and carries the parent's untouched sections by reference; whole restatement is permitted and never required. Where a supersession is a delta the parent still stands for everything the successor does not touch. — [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-adr-lifecycle-and-verification.md) (ADR lifecycle v2) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md)
- **Altitude** — A record decides; it does not enumerate. Counts, rosters and anything a compiler could check belong in tests and lint rules rather than in prose. — [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-adr-lifecycle-and-verification.md) (ADR lifecycle v2) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md)
- **Verification** — Machines are the gate; review is one bounded pass over the diff per step — no refutation rounds and no zero-finding requirement. Uncertain mechanics get a timeboxed spike in a worktree rather than a debate. — [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-adr-lifecycle-and-verification.md) (ADR lifecycle v2) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md)
- **The gate** — The gate command is defined once, in `CLAUDE.md` §Commands, and referenced by name everywhere else. `pnpm check` is the cached inner loop; a task whose result depends on anything outside the repository is never cached and declares its `env`. A cached task's hash covers every workspace whose source it runs: `test:unit` reaches its workspace dependencies through turbo's `transit` node, which no workspace defines as a script. — [ADR-0026](../adr/0026-task-graph-caching-and-serialisation.md) (turborepo task graph) as carried by [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-grid-and-admin-followups.md) and [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md), [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-grid-and-admin-followups.md) (grid and admin follow-ups) as carried by [ADR-0054](../adr/0054-design-language-instrument.md) and [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-impersonation-sessions.md) and [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-frontend-build-and-shared-composition.md), [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-impersonation-sessions.md) (impersonation sessions) as carried by [ADR-0067](../adr/0067-organizations.md) and [ADR-0070](../adr/0070-impersonation-in-a-new-tab.md) and [ADR-0071](../adr/0071-mail-flows.md) and [ADR-0072](../adr/0072-federated-identity-google-sign-in.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **The first link runs every check** — `lint`'s `dependsOn` carries every root and app check the repository defines — `test:scripts`, `docs:check`, `i18n:check` — and a hygiene case refuses a check it does not name, so a new one joins by predicate. A cached task's restored outputs must not decide its own result: a buildinfo sits under a cached output only beside the emit it belongs to. Coverage is reported with no threshold — on every run in the node suites, and in the jsdom suites only on `--coverage`, which keeps the slowest link a quarter shorter; `pnpm audit --prod` runs nightly beside the browser tier, reported and never gating. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **Pinning, holds and the cooldown** — Caret ranges by default and exact for the runtime framework and the compiler; any other exact pin is named with its reason in `renovate.json`'s pinning register. A version many workspaces declare lives in the `catalog:`; GitHub Actions are pinned by digest and the base images carry a named Renovate rule. A dependency held below a version is one `overrides` entry in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, not a pin per workspace. `minimumReleaseAge` is one day for pnpm and for Renovate alike, with the one-install override for a younger security fix written beside pnpm's setting, and a lockfile through review installs under `trustLockfile`. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **Forking** — A fork is a clone that keeps history, adds this repository as the `starter` remote and merges from it. A fork never edits an inherited record — it supersedes, because an edit turns the next merge into a conflict and erases which decision was deliberately dropped. `docs/adr/` and `.claude/` are carried into a fork; `docs/plan/` is this repository's journal and resets. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md)
- **Upstreaming** — A generic feature travels back re-implemented as its own deliverable off `starter/main`, never as a cherry-pick: the fork's diff is the specification, not the patch. Generic has a test — no fork domain nouns, and no reference to the fork's own record numbers or plan steps. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md)
- **Versioning** — `/ship` tags the shipping commit `starter-D<n>` and writes one changelog entry per shipped deliverable. Not per commit, and not semver. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md)
- **Citations that survive a fork** — In `.claude/**` every record citation carries a topic gloss and never a bare range, and no step numbers or dates appear. Source-code comments keep their step references — they are the reasoning attached to the code that carries it. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md)
- **The digests** — `docs/rules/<area>.md` states the rules currently in force, each line naming its record; the rule files and the skills load the digest for their area. The records remain the source of truth, and the digest is generated at ship rather than edited. The rule lines live in `scripts/rules-digest.mjs`, and the generator refuses an accepted record that no line cites as its own — accepting a record means writing its lines. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **Specs and notes** — A behaviour spec per capability in `docs/specs/` is current truth, edited in place with the behaviour and carried into forks like code. A plan file holds only what `/step` executes; the build notes go to its `.notes.md` sibling, so a builder opens the plan and one spec rather than the journal. — [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) (behaviour specs, and the plan apart from its notes)
